title.en: The empty language and the empty string

prompt.en:
Notation: Σ is a finite alphabet; a language is a set of strings over Σ. ε is the empty string. ∅ is the language with no strings at all. {ε} is the language whose only string is ε. For languages L and M, the concatenation L·M is the set of all strings xy with x in L and y in M. L* is the set of all concatenations of zero or more strings from L; zero strings give ε.

Which statement is true for every language L?
prompt.zh:
记号：Σ 是有限字母表；语言是 Σ 上字符串的集合。ε 是空串。∅ 是不含任何字符串的语言。{ε} 是只含 ε 一个字符串的语言。对语言 L 和 M，连接 L·M 是所有 xy 的集合，其中 x 属于 L、y 属于 M。L* 是 L 中零个或多个字符串连接而成的所有字符串的集合；零个字符串连接得到 ε。

下面哪个说法对每个语言 L 都成立？

why.en: There are no strings to concatenate, but "zero strings" is still allowed, and it gives ε. So ∅* contains ε.
why.zh: 虽然没有字符串可连接，但“零个字符串”仍然允许，它给出 ε。所以 ∅* 含有 ε。

why.en: A string of L·∅ needs a second part from ∅, and ∅ has none. So L·∅ = ∅, not L. It is {ε} that leaves L unchanged.
why.zh: L·∅ 中的串需要从 ∅ 取第二部分，而 ∅ 里没有串。所以 L·∅ = ∅，而不是 L。使 L 不变的是 {ε}。

why.en: Zero concatenations give ε, and no other string can be built from the strings of ∅. So ∅* = {ε}.
why.zh: 零次连接得到 ε，而 ∅ 里没有字符串，造不出别的串。所以 ∅* = {ε}。

why.en: Every string x of L gives εx = x, so {ε}·L = L. It is empty only if L is empty.
why.zh: L 中每个串 x 给出 εx = x，所以 {ε}·L = L。只有 L 本身为空时它才为空。

solution.en: The two special languages behave like the numbers 1 and 0 for concatenation: {ε} is the identity and ∅ wipes everything out. For star, the "zero copies" case always contributes ε.
solution.zh: 这两个特殊语言在连接运算中像数字 1 和 0：{ε} 是单位元，∅ 把一切抹掉。对于星运算，“零个”这一情形总会贡献 ε。

q.zh: 为什么零次重复很重要？

a.en: It adds ε even if the repeated block is nonempty.
a.zh: 即使重复的块是非空的，它也会把 ε 加进来。

q.en: Why does a modulo counter need few states?
q.zh: 为什么做模运算的计数器只需要很少的状态？

a.en: The question ignores complete totals and only needs a remainder.
a.zh: 这个问题不关心完整的总数，只需要一个余数。

q.en: Why can one failing branch be ignored?
q.zh: 为什么可以忽略一条失败的分支？

a.en: Acceptance requires at least one success, not success on every branch.
a.zh: 接受只要求至少有一次成功，而不要求每条分支都成功。

q.en: Why close after each ordinary move?
q.zh: 为什么每次普通转移之后都要取闭包？

a.en: The NFA may then take free moves before reading another symbol.
a.zh: 因为 NFA 在读入下一个符号之前，还可以先做免费的转移。

q.en: What does a missing loop contribute?
q.zh: 缺失的自环贡献了什么？

a.en: Its star contributes ε, representing zero visits around the loop.
a.zh: 它的星贡献 ε，表示绕这个环零次。

q.en: Why can a short pattern be slow?
q.zh: 为什么一个很短的模式也可能很慢？

a.en: Its execution may revisit many decompositions that lead to the same failure.
a.zh: 它的执行可能重复探索许多种分解，而它们最终都导向同样的失败。

prompt.en:
Notation: Σ is a finite alphabet; Σ* is the set of all strings over Σ. L1 is a regular language over Σ and L2 is a nonregular language over Σ. Regular languages are closed under union, intersection, complement and concatenation.

Which of the following languages is guaranteed to be nonregular, whatever L1 and L2 are?
prompt.zh:
记号：Σ 是有限字母表，Σ* 是 Σ 上所有字符串的集合。L1 是 Σ 上的正则语言，L2 是 Σ 上的非正则语言。正则语言对并、交、补和连接封闭。

无论 L1 和 L2 是什么，下面哪个语言一定非正则？

why.en: It can be regular. Take L1 = Σ*; then L1 ∪ L2 = Σ*, which is regular.
why.zh: 它可以是正则的。取 L1 = Σ*，则 L1 ∪ L2 = Σ*，是正则的。

why.en: It can be regular. Take L1 = ∅; then the intersection is ∅.
why.zh: 它可以是正则的。取 L1 = ∅，则交集是 ∅。

why.en: It can be regular. Take L1 = ∅; then L1·L2 = ∅.
why.zh: 它可以是正则的。取 L1 = ∅，则 L1·L2 = ∅。

why.en: If the complement were regular, then its complement, which is L2, would be regular too, because regular languages are closed under complement. That contradicts the assumption. So Σ* ∖ L2 is always nonregular.
why.zh: 若补语言是正则的，那么它的补语言，即 L2，也是正则的，因为正则语言对补封闭。这与假设矛盾。所以 Σ* ∖ L2 一定非正则。

solution.en: Only complement is a reversible operation here: complementing twice returns the original language. Union, intersection and concatenation can lose information, for example when L1 is ∅ or Σ*.
solution.zh: 这里只有补运算是可逆的：补两次就回到原语言。并、交和连接可能丢失信息，例如当 L1 是 ∅ 或 Σ* 时。

title.en: Which language needs only finite memory?
title.zh: 哪个语言只需要有限记忆？

prompt.en:
Notation: over Σ = {a,b}, #a(w) and #b(w) are the numbers of a's and b's in w. A prefix of w is any initial segment of w, including ε and w itself. wᴿ is w written backwards.

Exactly one of the languages below is regular. Which one?
prompt.zh:
记号：在 Σ = {a,b} 上，#a(w) 和 #b(w) 分别是 w 中 a 与 b 的个数。w 的前缀是 w 的任一开头部分，包括 ε 和 w 本身。wᴿ 是把 w 倒过来写。

下面的语言恰有一个是正则的，是哪一个？

text.en: { w : for every prefix x of w, |#a(x) − #b(x)| ≤ 2 }
text.zh: { w : 对 w 的每个前缀 x，|#a(x) − #b(x)| ≤ 2 }

why.en: The running difference is only ever in {−2,…,2}. Five states record it, one dead state records "the bound was broken", and every state is accepting except the dead one. A finite summary suffices.
why.zh: 运行中的差值只在 {−2,…,2} 内。五个状态记录它，一个死状态记录“界限已被突破”，除死状态外全部接受。有限的摘要就够了。

why.en: An automaton must remember n while reading a, then count 2n b's. n is unbounded, so no finite set of states is enough (the same argument as for aⁿbⁿ).
why.zh: 自动机读 a 时必须记住 n，之后还要数 2n 个 b。n 没有上界，有限个状态不够用（论证与 aⁿbⁿ 相同）。

why.en: The difference #a − #b can be any integer, and different differences need different future behaviour. Infinitely many distinctions mean no DFA. (Intersecting with a*b* gives aⁿbⁿ.)
why.zh: 差值 #a − #b 可以是任意整数，不同差值对应不同的后续行为。需要区分无穷多种情形，所以没有 DFA。（与 a*b* 取交集得到 aⁿbⁿ。）

why.en: To check a palindrome, the machine must remember the first half of the input, which is unbounded. Two long prefixes that differ need different continuations, so no DFA.
why.zh: 判断回文必须记住前半段，而它的长度无界。两个不同的长前缀需要不同的后续，所以没有 DFA。

solution.en: "Counting" is regular only when the count stays inside a fixed window. A bounded difference is a finite set of states; an unbounded one is not.
solution.zh: “计数”只有在计数值始终落在固定范围内时才是正则的。有界的差值就是有限个状态，无界的差值则不是。

q.en: Why can a finite grammar generate infinitely many strings?
q.zh: 为什么有限的文法能生成无穷多个字符串？

a.en: A recursive rule can be applied any finite number of times.
a.zh: 一条递归的规则可以被应用任意有限多次。

prompt.en:
Notation: a grammar lists rules "Variable → alternatives", separated by |. S is the start variable and a, b are terminals. ε in a rule means the empty right-hand side. A grammar is ambiguous when some string has two different parse trees.

Exactly one of these grammars is ambiguous. Which one?
prompt.zh:
记号：文法用“变量 → 若干选择”的形式列出规则，选择之间用 | 隔开。S 是起始变量，a、b 是终结符。规则中的 ε 表示空的右侧。若某个字符串有两棵不同的解析树，文法就有歧义。

下面的文法恰有一个有歧义，是哪一个？

why.en: Every string aⁿbⁿ has one tree: n uses of aSb followed by ε. Nothing else can be chosen at each step.
why.zh: 每个字符串 aⁿbⁿ 只有一棵树：用 n 次 aSb 再用 ε。每一步都没有别的选择。

why.en: The string aab has two parse trees: S ⇒ aS ⇒ aSb ⇒ aab (the a-rule applied first) and S ⇒ Sb ⇒ aSb ⇒ aab (the b-rule applied first). The order of the two recursive rules is not forced.
why.zh: 字符串 aab 有两棵解析树：S ⇒ aS ⇒ aSb ⇒ aab（先用 a 规则），以及 S ⇒ Sb ⇒ aSb ⇒ aab（先用 b 规则）。两个递归规则的先后没有被强制。

why.en: The first symbol of the string decides the rule at each step, and ε is used only at the end. One tree per string.
why.zh: 每一步由字符串的第一个符号决定用哪条规则，ε 只在最后使用。每个字符串只有一棵树。

text.en: S → AB, A → aA | ε, B → bB | ε
text.zh: S → AB, A → aA | ε, B → bB | ε

why.en: A produces exactly the leading a's and B the trailing b's, so each string aⁱbʲ has one tree. Having ε-rules does not by itself make a grammar ambiguous.
why.zh: A 恰好产生开头的 a，B 恰好产生结尾的 b，所以每个字符串 aⁱbʲ 只有一棵树。含有 ε 规则本身并不会使文法有歧义。

solution.en: To test ambiguity, look for a string where two rules can be applied in either order, or where one rule can cover the same part in two ways. The first grammar has two recursive rules (aS and Sb) that can both be applied to the same variable, while the others always have only one possible choice.
solution.zh: 检验歧义时，找一个字符串：其中两条规则可以按任意先后使用，或一条规则能以两种方式覆盖同一部分。第一个文法有两条递归规则（aS 和 Sb）都能用在同一个变量上，其余文法每一步都只有一种可能的选择。

title.en: Which grammar is in Chomsky normal form?
title.zh: 哪个文法是 Chomsky 范式？

prompt.en:
Notation: S is the start variable; lowercase letters are terminals and capital letters are variables. ε is the empty right-hand side. A grammar is in Chomsky normal form (CNF) when every rule has the form A → BC (two variables) or A → a (one terminal). In addition, S → ε is allowed only if S does not occur on the right-hand side of any rule.

Which grammar is in CNF?
prompt.zh:
记号：S 是起始变量；小写字母是终结符，大写字母是变量。ε 表示空的右侧。文法是 Chomsky 范式（CNF），当且仅当每条规则都形如 A → BC（两个变量）或 A → a（一个终结符）。另外，只有当 S 不出现在任何规则的右侧时，才允许 S → ε。

哪个文法是 CNF？

why.en: S → aB mixes a terminal with a variable. CNF needs a helper variable for the terminal.
why.zh: S → aB 把终结符和变量混在一起。CNF 需要为终结符引入辅助变量。

text.en: S → AB | a;  A → SB | b;  B → AA | a
text.zh: S → AB | a;  A → SB | b;  B → AA | a

why.en: Every rule is A → BC or A → a. S appears on a right-hand side, but this is harmless because there is no S → ε. This is CNF.
why.zh: 每条规则都是 A → BC 或 A → a。S 出现在右侧，但没有 S → ε，所以没有问题。这是 CNF。

text.en: S → ABC | a;  A → a;  B → b;  C → a
text.zh: S → ABC | a;  A → a;  B → b;  C → a

why.en: S → ABC has three variables on the right. CNF allows exactly two.
why.zh: S → ABC 右侧有三个变量，CNF 恰好允许两个。

text.en: S → A | AB;  A → a;  B → b
text.zh: S → A | AB;  A → a;  B → b

why.en: S → A is a unit rule (one variable on the right). CNF forbids it.
why.zh: S → A 是单位规则（右侧只有一个变量），CNF 不允许。

text.en: S → AB | ε;  A → SB | b;  B → a
text.zh: S → AB | ε;  A → SB | b;  B → a

why.en: S → ε is allowed only when S never appears on a right-hand side. Here A → SB uses S on the right, so this is not CNF. A fresh start variable would be needed.
why.zh: 只有当 S 从不出现在右侧时才允许 S → ε。这里 A → SB 的右侧用了 S，所以不是 CNF。需要引入一个新的起始变量。

solution.en: Check each rule one by one: two variables, or one terminal. The ε exception for the start variable is the only place where the position of S matters.
solution.zh: 逐条规则检查：要么两个变量，要么一个终结符。起始变量的 ε 例外是唯一与 S 的位置有关的地方。

q.en: Why store a set in each cell?
q.zh: 为什么每个格子里要存一个集合？

a.en: Several variables may derive the same substring and be useful in different parent rules.
a.zh: 几个变量可能推导出同一个子串，并且在不同的父规则中都有用。

q.en: Why is state alone not a configuration?
q.zh: 为什么只有状态还不是一个配置？

a.en: The same state can read different cells or symbols and therefore have different next steps.
a.zh: 同一个状态可能读到不同的格子或不同的符号，因此下一步也会不同。

q.en: Why are marker symbols useful even though states can remember information?
q.zh: 状态本来就能记住信息，为什么标记符号还是有用的？

a.en: Markers preserve an unbounded number of local facts on the tape. A fixed finite state set cannot remember an arbitrary collection of visited positions.
a.zh: 标记在纸带上保存了数量没有上限的局部事实。一个固定的有限状态集合，无法记住任意一批被访问过的位置。

q.en: What do the three parts of the label 1/0,L mean?
q.zh: 标签 1/0,L 的三部分各是什么意思？

a.en: Read 1, write 0, move the head one cell to the left.
a.zh: 读到 1，写下 0，磁头向左移动一格。

title.en: What does "equivalent" mean for a multitape machine?
title.zh: 多带图灵机“等价”是什么意思？

prompt.en:
Notation: a k-tape Turing machine has k tapes, each with its own head, and one finite control that reads all k symbols at once. A single-tape machine has one tape and one head. Two machine models are equivalent if they decide the same class of languages and recognize the same class of languages.

Which statement about two-tape and single-tape machines is correct?
prompt.zh:
记号：k 带图灵机有 k 条纸带，每条带有自己的读写头，只有一个有限控制，它一次读取全部 k 个符号。单带机器只有一条纸带和一个读写头。若两种机器模型能判定同一类语言、能识别同一类语言，它们就是等价的。

关于双带机器与单带机器，哪个说法正确？

text.en: Two-tape machines can decide some languages that no single-tape machine can.
text.zh: 双带机器能判定某些任何单带机器都不能判定的语言。

why.en: A single-tape machine can simulate two tapes by keeping both contents on one tape (with markers for the two head positions). The class of languages stays the same.
why.zh: 单带机器可以把两条带的内容放在同一条带上（用标记表示两个读写头的位置）来模拟。语言类不变。

text.en: A single-tape machine can simulate a two-tape machine, but it may take more steps.
text.zh: 单带机器可以模拟双带机器，但可能需要更多步。

why.en: Right. Each simulated step requires scanning the whole used part of the tape to find the two marked head positions, so time may grow (by a polynomial factor), but the languages decided are the same.
why.zh: 对。每个被模拟的步骤都需要扫描纸带的已用部分来找到两个被标记的读写头位置，所以时间可能增加（多项式倍），但所判定的语言相同。

text.en: "Equivalent" means that the two machines always use the same number of steps.
text.zh: “等价”意味着两台机器总是用相同的步数。

why.en: Equivalence is about which languages and functions can be computed, not about speed. Step counts can differ.
why.zh: 等价说的是能计算哪些语言和函数，而不是速度。步数可以不同。

text.en: Simulation needs a single-tape machine with an infinite tape alphabet.
text.zh: 模拟需要带字母表为无穷的单带机器。

why.en: A finite alphabet suffices: store the pair of symbols in each cell as one new symbol, or interleave the contents. The alphabet of any Turing machine is finite.
why.zh: 有限字母表就够了：把每格中的符号对当成一个新符号，或交错存放两条带的内容。任何图灵机的字母表都是有限的。

solution.en: Variants such as extra tapes, a stay move, or a two-way tape change the descriptions and the speed, not what can be computed. The Church–Turing thesis relies on exactly this kind of robustness.
solution.zh: 额外的纸带、原地不动的移动、双向纸带等变体改变的是描述和速度，而不是可计算的范围。Church–Turing 论题正是依赖这种稳健性。

title.en: Does a looping recognizer prove undecidability?
title.zh: 会无限循环的识别器能证明不可判定吗？

prompt.en:
Notation: a recognizer for L halts and accepts every string in L and never accepts a string outside L; on other strings it may reject or run forever. A decider for L halts on every input and says yes exactly for the strings of L.

Mia writes a Turing machine M that accepts every string of a language L, never accepts a string outside L, but runs forever on the input 101 (which is not in L). Mia concludes "so L is undecidable". How good is her conclusion?
prompt.zh:
记号：L 的识别器对 L 中的每个字符串停机并接受，对 L 之外的字符串从不接受；对其他字符串它可以拒绝，也可以永远运行。L 的判定器对每个输入都停机，并且恰对 L 中的字符串回答 yes。

Mia 写了一台图灵机 M：它接受 L 中的每个字符串，从不接受 L 之外的字符串，但对输入 101（101 不在 L 中）会永远运行。Mia 因此得出结论：“所以 L 不可判定”。她的结论怎么样？

text.en: Incorrect: M is only a recognizer; some other machine might still decide L.
text.zh: 不正确：M 只是识别器；也许另有一台机器能判定 L。

why.en: Right. M's looping on 101 says nothing about L itself. L might be a simple regular language for which a different machine always halts. To prove undecidability, one must rule out every machine.
why.zh: 对。M 在 101 上循环，并不说明 L 本身有什么问题。L 可能是个简单的正则语言，换一台机器就总能停机。要证明不可判定，必须排除所有机器。

text.en: Correct: a decider must halt on every input, and M does not.
text.zh: 正确：判定器必须对每个输入停机，而 M 做不到。

why.en: This shows only that M is not a decider. Undecidability says that no machine at all decides L, and Mia has looked at one machine.
why.zh: 这只说明 M 不是判定器。不可判定是指没有任何机器能判定 L，而 Mia 只看了一台机器。

text.en: Correct: L must then have a complement that is not recognizable.
text.zh: 正确：这样 L 的补语言必定不可识别。

why.en: No such implication holds. If L is decidable, its complement is decidable and so recognizable.
why.zh: 没有这样的推论。若 L 可判定，它的补语言也可判定，从而可识别。

text.en: Incorrect: adding a step counter to M makes it halt on all inputs, so L is decidable.
text.zh: 不正确：给 M 加一个步数计数器就能使它对所有输入停机，所以 L 可判定。

why.en: A counter would have to choose a limit and then reject. On a string of L that needs more steps than the limit, M would then reject wrongly.
why.zh: 计数器必须选定一个上限，然后拒绝。对于 L 中需要更多步才能接受的字符串，M 就会错误地拒绝。

solution.en: "This machine loops" is a fact about one machine. "No machine decides L" is a fact about every machine. The first never proves the second.
solution.zh: “这台机器会循环”是关于某一台机器的事实，“没有机器能判定 L”是关于所有机器的事实。前者不能推出后者。

title.en: The complement of a recognizable, undecidable language
title.zh: 可识别但不可判定的语言的补语言

prompt.en:
Notation: L is recognizable if some Turing machine accepts exactly the strings of L (it may run forever on others). L is decidable if some Turing machine halts on every input and accepts exactly the strings of L. L̄ = Σ* ∖ L is the complement of L.

Suppose L is recognizable but not decidable. What can you say about L̄?
prompt.zh:
记号：若某台图灵机恰好接受 L 的字符串（对其他字符串可以永远运行），L 就是可识别的。若某台图灵机对每个输入都停机并且恰好接受 L 的字符串，L 就是可判定的。L̄ = Σ* ∖ L 是 L 的补语言。

假设 L 可识别但不可判定。关于 L̄ 你能说什么？

why.en: If L̄ were decidable, swapping yes and no would decide L. But L is not decidable.
why.zh: 若 L̄ 可判定，交换 yes 和 no 就能判定 L，而 L 不可判定。

text.en: L̄ is recognizable but not decidable.
text.zh: L̄ 可识别但不可判定。

why.en: If L̄ were recognizable, then running recognizers for L and L̄ side by side would decide L (one of them must accept). So L̄ cannot be recognizable.
why.zh: 若 L̄ 可识别，把 L 和 L̄ 的识别器并行运行就能判定 L（二者必有一个接受）。所以 L̄ 不可能可识别。

text.en: Nothing can be said; L̄ may be recognizable or not.
text.zh: 无法判断；L̄ 可能可识别，也可能不可识别。

why.en: The theorem "L decidable iff L and L̄ both recognizable" settles it: here L̄ is certainly not recognizable.
why.zh: 定理“L 可判定当且仅当 L 和 L̄ 都可识别”已经给出结论：这里 L̄ 必定不可识别。

why.en: Correct: if both L and L̄ were recognizable, interleaving the two recognizers would give a decider for L. Since L is undecidable, L̄ is not recognizable.
why.zh: 对：若 L 和 L̄ 都可识别，交错运行两个识别器就得到 L 的判定器。L 不可判定，所以 L̄ 不可识别。

solution.en: Think of the pair {L, L̄}: if both halves can be recognized, one of the two recognizers always says yes, so together they decide. Undecidable L therefore breaks at least one half.
solution.zh: 把 {L, L̄} 看成一对：若两半都能识别，两个识别器中总有一个会说 yes，合起来就是判定器。所以 L 不可判定，就至少有一半不可识别。

q.en: Why must we prove both directions of “M accepts w exactly when S accepts”?
q.zh: 为什么要证明“M 接受 w 当且仅当 S 接受”的两个方向？

a.en: With only one direction, S could still be wrong on some inputs, for example rejecting a pair that M really accepts. Then S would not decide A_TM.
a.zh: 只证一个方向的话，S 仍可能在某些输入上出错，比如拒绝了 M 确实接受的二元组。那样 S 就没有判定 A_TM。

q.en: Why are there eight rows for three atoms?
q.zh: 为什么三个原子命题有八行？

a.en: Each has two choices, so 2×2×2=8 assignments.
a.zh: 每一个有两种选择，所以有 2×2×2=8 个赋值。

title.en: Which formula is equivalent to p → (q → r)?
title.zh: 哪个公式与 p → (q → r) 等价？

prompt.en:
Notation: two formulas are equivalent when they have the same truth value under every truth assignment. → is "if … then" and is false only when the left side is true and the right side is false. → is not associative: p → (q → r) and (p → q) → r are different.

Which formula is equivalent to p → (q → r)?
prompt.zh:
记号：两个公式在每个真值赋值下真值都相同，就是等价的。→ 是“如果……那么”，仅当左边为真而右边为假时才为假。→ 不满足结合律：p → (q → r) 与 (p → q) → r 不同。

哪个公式与 p → (q → r) 等价？

why.en: Not equivalent. With p = F, q = F, r = F the original is true, but (p → q) → r is T → F, which is false.
why.zh: 不等价。取 p = F，q = F，r = F，原公式为真，而 (p → q) → r 是 T → F，为假。

why.en: Not equivalent. With p = T, q = F, r = T the original is true (q → r has a false left side), but p → (q ∧ r) is false.
why.zh: 不等价。取 p = T，q = F，r = T，原公式为真（q → r 的左边为假），而 p → (q ∧ r) 为假。

why.en: Both are false exactly when p and q are true and r is false. (This is "currying": assume p, then assume q.)
why.zh: 二者都恰在 p、q 为真而 r 为假时为假。（这就是“柯里化”：先假设 p，再假设 q。）

why.en: Not equivalent. With p = F, q = T, r = F the original is true (p is false), but (p ∨ q) → r is false.
why.zh: 不等价。取 p = F，q = T，r = F：原公式因 p 为假而为真，而 (p ∨ q) → r 为假。

solution.en: Find the single falsifying case of the original: p true, q true, r false. The right answer must be false there and nowhere else.
solution.zh: 先找到原公式唯一的使其为假的情形：p 真、q 真、r 假。正确的选项必须恰在这一种情形下为假。

a.en: Yes. A single literal is a one-literal clause.
a.zh: 是的。一个单独的文字就是只含一个文字的子句。

prompt.en:
Notation: Γ ⊨ F means every truth assignment that makes all formulas of Γ true also makes F true. p, q, r are atoms; ∨ is "or", ∧ is "and", ¬ is "not", → is "if … then", ↔ is "if and only if".

Exactly one of these claims is valid. Which one?
prompt.zh:
记号：Γ ⊨ F 表示凡使 Γ 中所有公式为真的真值赋值，也使 F 为真。p、q、r 是原子命题；∨ 是“或”，∧ 是“且”，¬ 是“非”，→ 是“如果……那么”，↔ 是“当且仅当”。

下面的断言恰有一个成立，是哪一个？

why.en: Case on p. If p is true, ¬p is false so ¬p ∨ r forces r. If p is false, p ∨ q forces q. Either way q ∨ r holds. This is the resolution rule.
why.zh: 对 p 分情况。若 p 为真，¬p 为假，所以 ¬p ∨ r 迫使 r 为真。若 p 为假，p ∨ q 迫使 q 为真。两种情况下 q ∨ r 都成立。这就是归结规则。

why.en: Countermodel: p = F, q = T. Then p → q is true and q → p is false. The converse of an implication is not implied by it.
why.zh: 反模型：p = F，q = T。此时 p → q 为真，q → p 为假。从 p → q 推不出它的逆命题 q → p。

why.en: Countermodel: p = T, q = T, r = F. The premise is true, but p → r is false. "Q or R" does not give both.
why.zh: 反模型：p = T，q = T，r = F。前提为真，但 p → r 为假。“q 或 r”推不出 q 和 r 两者都成立。

why.en: Countermodel: p = F, q = F, r = T. Both premises are true, since p ↔ q has equal values and q ∨ r has r, but p is false.
why.zh: 反模型：p = F，q = F，r = T。两个前提都为真（p ↔ q 两边值相同，q ∨ r 靠 r 为真），但 p 为假。

solution.en: To refute an entailment, one countermodel is enough: premises true, conclusion false. To confirm it, argue over all cases or show that premises together with ¬F cannot all be true.
solution.zh: 要驳倒一个后承，一个反模型就够了：前提为真而结论为假。要确认它成立，则要对所有情形论证，或说明前提加上 ¬F 不可能同时为真。

title.en: Choose the formula with the right quantifier scope
title.zh: 选出量词作用域正确的公式

prompt.en:
Notation: the domain contains students and courses. Student(x) means x is a student, Course(y) means y is a course, and Takes(x,y) means x takes y. ∀ is "for all", ∃ is "there exists", → is "if … then", ∧ is "and".

Which formula says exactly "Every student takes at least one course"? (The course may differ from student to student.)
prompt.zh:
记号：论域包含学生和课程。Student(x) 表示 x 是学生，Course(y) 表示 y 是课程，Takes(x,y) 表示 x 选修 y。∀ 是“对所有”，∃ 是“存在”，→ 是“如果……那么”，∧ 是“且”。

哪个公式恰好表示“每个学生至少选修一门课”？（课程可以因学生而异。）

why.en: With ∧ directly under ∀x, it claims that every object x in the domain is a student. Courses would also have to be students. It is too strong.
why.zh: ∧ 直接放在 ∀x 之下，等于声称论域里每个对象 x 都是学生，课程也得是学生。这太强了。

why.en: Putting ∃y first forces one single course that all students take. That is stronger than the claim.
why.zh: 把 ∃y 放在最前，就强制存在同一门所有学生都选的课，比原命题强。

why.en: This says every student takes every course. The inner quantifier should be ∃, not ∀.
why.zh: 这表示每个学生选修每门课。内层量词应该是 ∃ 而不是 ∀。

why.en: The implication restricts x to students. The inner ∃y sits after x, so the course can depend on x, and ∧ inside the ∃ says y is a course that x takes. This is right.
why.zh: 蕴含把 x 限制为学生。内层的 ∃y 在 x 之后，所以课程可以依赖于 x；∃ 里面的 ∧ 表示 y 是 x 选修的课程。这是对的。

solution.en: Read from the left: the quantifiers fix who may depend on whom. The student x is chosen first, then a course y may be found for that x. ∀ pairs with → to restrict a group; ∃ pairs with ∧ to name a witness.
solution.zh: 从左往右读：量词的顺序决定谁可以依赖谁。先选定学生 x，再为这个 x 找课程 y。∀ 与 → 搭配来限定一类对象，∃ 与 ∧ 搭配来指出见证。

q.en: Why does “every A is B” use → and not ∧?
q.zh: 为什么“每个 A 都是 B”用 → 而不用 ∧？

a.en: The claim is only about things that are A. For anything that is not A, the implication is true and does no harm. With ∧ the formula would say that everything is both A and B.
a.zh: 这句话只涉及属于 A 的东西。对于不属于 A 的东西，蕴含为真，不会造成妨碍。如果用 ∧，公式就变成了“所有东西既是 A 又是 B”。

q.en: Why does this proof require H to halt on every input?
q.zh: 为什么这个证明要求 H 在每一个输入上都停机？

a.en: D must receive H’s answer before choosing its opposite behavior. If H can loop or say unknown, the contradiction no longer establishes a complete decision procedure.
a.zh: D 必须先收到 H 的答案，才能选择与之相反的行为。如果 H 可以循环，或者可以回答“未知”，这个矛盾就不再能说明不存在一个完整的判定过程。
